{library.search} searches as you type. T: {library.search} searches as you type. The arrow keys, or {library.left} {library.down} {library.up} {library.right}, move around the shelf, and {library.read} opens the selected book where you left off.

{library.sites} connects Goodreads, Open Library or Hardcover: what you read, are reading and want to read comes in with your stars and dates. Nothing is removed, and nothing goes back unless you turn that on.
{library.sites} lists Goodreads, Open Li: {library.sites} lists Goodreads, Open Library and Hardcover, each not connected, connected as somebody, or needing attention. Paste a link to your profile, a shelf, or your user name: Omabook looks at once and says what it found, or exactly why not. Sync brings your shelves in; books you own on paper become paper books, and the rest books you know of.
{library.sort} changes the order and {li: {library.sort} changes the order and {library.sort_reverse} turns it round. {library.filter} filters: type a few letters of a status, a format, a language, a tag, an author, a series or a rating, and Enter takes the match. Filters add up and show as chips; {library.filter_clear} takes them all off.
{library.stats} shows the time you read,: {library.stats} shows the time you read, the days in a row and the books finished, by month and by book, and how far you are with a goal for the year. It is all counted on your computer.
{library.subscribe} takes a collection s: {library.subscribe} takes a collection someone shared: the books you have are matched, the others become wishes, and its graph shows only as far as you have read each book yourself.
{library.subscribe} takes such a file, o: {library.subscribe} takes such a file, one dropped on the window, or a link. Before anything is written it says which of its books you have and which become wishlist entries, in a collection of yours. The shared space stays apart, read-only, and is never merged into your library. Unsubscribing drops it and keeps your collection.
{library.suggest} suggests books from ev: {library.suggest} suggests books from everything you have read, on paper too, and checks each one against the reading sites.
{library.sync} brings this library and a: {library.sync} brings this library and another computer's in step over ssh; the later reading place wins.
{library.tidy} finds the same book twice: {library.tidy} finds the same book twice, authors spelled several ways and books that belong to a series, as one list to tick. Nothing changes until you say so.
{library.view_covers} to {library.view_s: {library.view_covers} to {library.view_stacks} show the shelf as covers, spines, a carousel, a list or stacks, and {library.view_next} goes to the next. In stacks, {library.group} piles by series, author, tag or reading status.
{reader.ask} asks about what you are rea: {reader.ask} asks about what you are reading, {reader.catch_up} catches you up after a break, and {reader.cast} says who is who. It is sent the book only as far as you have read.
{reader.ask} opens the companion beside: {reader.ask} opens the companion beside the page. Ask about the chapter in front of you, or select a passage first and ask about that. It is sent the book only as far as you have read, so it can't spoil the ending.
{reader.catch_up} tells you where things: {reader.catch_up} tells you where things stand, in a few lines. {reader.cast} lists the people and places that matter so far. Both keep notes with the book, so a later book in a series builds on the earlier ones.
{reader.contents} shows the chapters bes: {reader.contents} shows the chapters beside the page, and {reader.find} finds words in the book. {reader.bookmark} keeps a bookmark. Your place is remembered when you leave with {reader.back}.
{reader.contents} shows the chapters beside the page. {reader.find} finds words in the book.
{reader.expand} hides everything but the: {reader.expand} hides everything but the book, and {reader.back} goes back to the shelf. {global.help} has the rest.
{reader.find} finds the words in your hi: {reader.find} finds the words in your highlights, margin notes and bookmarks too, listed before the book's own; start with `notes:` to look only there. In the library, `notes:` finds the books you wrote the words in. Where a model reads your handwriting (recognition, in the settings), ink on the pages is found by its words as well; it goes only to your own servers.
{reader.format} opens the Aa panel besid: {reader.format} opens the Aa panel beside the page (Aa in the bar, with fingers): the font, its size, the longest line in characters, the pages side by side, the space between lines and between paragraphs, a first-line indent, the margins, and the alignment: start, justified (filled out to both sides), centred or end. Each change shows at once and the page stays where you were. With Only this book on, the change is for this book alone; Reset puts back what there was when the panel opened. The defaults for every book are in the settings ({global.settings}) too. Pages that are pictures, as in a PDF or a comic, can't be set. Their layout can.

{reader.format} opens the Aa panel beside the page: the font and its size, the widest line, the spacing, an indent, the margins, and text justified, centred or to either side. For every book, or only this one.
{reader.ink} writes and draws on the pag: {reader.ink} writes and draws on the pages of a PDF or a comic, with a pen or the mouse. In other books a pen writes a margin note on the line, read by your own AI server so the book's search finds it.
{reader.larger} and {reader.smaller} cha: {reader.larger} and {reader.smaller} change the size of the type. {reader.expand} shows the book and nothing else, on the whole screen.
{reader.layout} chooses how a book is re: {reader.layout} chooses how a book is read through, also under Layout in the Aa panel. Pages: even one column is cut into pages, each chapter starts on a page of its own, and turning on from its last page opens the next chapter; a PDF or comic page is shown whole, and two side by side open as a book does, page 1 alone (First page alone). Scroll: one column that runs on, with a line at each chapter's end saying what is next; scroll on past it, or tap it, to go on. Automatic: pages where two fit side by side, else a column that scrolls. Your place stays where it is when you change.
{reader.layout} reads a book as pages, e: {reader.layout} reads a book as pages, each chapter starting on a page of its own and a PDF page shown whole, or as one column that runs on from chapter to chapter. A turn never shows a line twice.
{reader.note} writes a note on the selec: {reader.note} writes a note on the selected words, beside them where the window has room, and {reader.notes} goes through the page's notes. Notes and highlights are found again by their words when a book's file changes.
{reader.page_down} turns the page and ca: {reader.page_down} turns the page and carries on into the next chapter; {reader.page_up} goes back. {reader.larger} and {reader.smaller} change the size of the type.
{reader.page_down} turns the page, or sc: {reader.page_down} turns the page, or scrolls a screen on, and carries on into the next chapter; {reader.page_up} goes back. Nothing is shown twice: the next screen starts at the first line that wasn't wholly in sight. {reader.next} goes to the next chapter; {reader.previous} to the start of this one, and from there to the one before. {reader.line_down} and {reader.line_up} scroll a few lines. Where the window has room, two or three pages stand side by side and a turn moves on by all of them; otherwise one page scrolls.
